You can use your <b>Barrier Skill</> to temporarily boost your defense.

Use the <b>Barrier</> Skill (<gga id="bp_bga_player_generic_barrier_p"/>)  to actively defend yourself, granting extra protection.

Equipping a shield or wearing certain armor types increases your ability to do this effectively.

Ailments are <b>negative effects</> that can be applied as <b>stacks</> to enemies and players.

There are 3 steps when applying Ailments:
• <b>Attack:</> Each attack has an Ailment-Chance, that defines if it would apply an Ailment. 
• <b>Resist:</> The target now resists the Ailment being applied by using its Resistances.
• <b>Define Type:</> If an Ailment is applied and the creature doesn’t resist, the <b>type of Ailment</> is chosen. It depends on the attack’s <b>damage-types</>. The <b>more damage</> of a type is present, the <b>higher the chance</> of its Ailment being applied.

Should Ailment-Chance be <b>above 100%</>, an <b>additional roll</> in the “Define Type” step is made to maybe apply a <b>2nd stack</> and so on.

Ailments are applied as <b>stacks</>.
Each stack <b>expires</> after a certain <b>duration</>.
The <b>maximum amount</> of stacks per Ailment is <b>10</> per creature or player applying it. It can never exceed <b>20</>, even from multiple sources combined.
Each Ailment has a <b>different effect</> once applied.
The <b>strength</> of this effect is defined by the <b>amount of stacks</> on the target.

The following Ailments exist:
• <b>Stagger</> is caused by <b>Strike Damage</> and reduces the targets <b>move and attack-speed</>.
• <b>Bleeding</> is caused by <b>Pierce Damage</> and causes the target to receive <b>Damage over Time</> (DoT).
• <b>Burning</> is caused by <b>Fire Damage</> and causes the target to receive <b>DoT</>.
• <b>Chilled</> is caused by <b>Cold Damage</> and causes the target to receive <b>low DoT (half compared to main-damaging Ailments) and be slowed</>.
• <b>Plagued</> is caused by <b>Poison Damage</> and causes the target to receive <b>DoT</>.
• <b>Shocked</> is caused by <b>Lightning Damage</> and causes the target to receive <b>DoT</> and be have a chance of being <b>disrupted</> when performing abilities.

Any Ailment damage is dealt as <b>True Damage</> and is <b>not adjusted by Resistances</>.

Each attack has a chance for a <b>Critical Hit</>. Critical Hits deal <b>higher damage</> and have a <b>higher chance to apply Ailments</>.
The chance for this is defined by the following aspects:

• The attack’s Critical Hit <b>base chance</>.
• Weapon Attacks add the <b>weapon’s Critical Hit Chance</>.
• Any Critical Hit Chance modifiers from <b>gear or abilities</>.

<b>Supercrits:</> If the Critical Hit Chance of an attack is <b>above 100%</> it can Supercrit.
Any %-points above 100 form the chance of the Supercrit occuring.
Supercrits have an even <b>higher damage and Ailment chance</>.

There are <b>multiple ways</> to defend against enemy attacks.

The following elements work <b>in order</> as described whenever damage is applied:
• <b>Glancing:</> %-based defense. If the glancing roll is successful it reduces the incoming damage and offensive effects of the attack.
• <b>Protection and Damage Reduction:</> Any  damage-reducing effects from gear or abilities apply. 
• <b>Resistances:</> Reduce any non-physical damage based on type.
• <b>Armor:</> Reduces physical damage based on type.
• <b>Shielding Effects:</> Lastly any additional shielding effects like Barrier absorb damage.

They can be <b>customized individually</>. 
This can be helpful when using different weapons via <b>weapon swap</>.
The points are <b>not shared</> between the two abilities and need to be assigned seperately.

The power of the <b>Dye Phial</> allows you to absorb <b>Nemesis Energy</>.\r\nWhenever you do, the absorbed energy enters the phial.\r\nOnce it is full, the energy will disappear, leaving the phial empty and granting you <b>Divinity</>.
You have found a piece of a <b>Relic</> or <b>Charm</>!\r\nThey are stored in their own tab in your inventory.\r\nCharms and Relics can be <b>slotted into your items</> to add their effects.

You can <b>combine</> up to 3 pieces of the same Charm or Relic of the same rarity for <b>stronger effects</>.\r\nOnce <b>fully assembled</> they gain a <b>completion bonus</>.\r\nThe <b>amount</> of Charms and Relics you can equip depends on your <b>character\'s level</>.

Make sure to gather them during combat.

You have just unlocked a <b>Sustained Skill</>.\r\nThese skills <b>are not cast directly</> but instead <b>reserve</> either Energy or Health.\r\nTo activate or deactivate sustained skills press the button in the Mastery screen.

You can enable or disable <b>Sustained Skills</> here.
Some <b>Sustained Skills</> (like Summons) also have an active ability.
These can be used normally by dragging the skill into your skill-bar from the Mastery Screen.
Any active abilities can only be used, if the skill is activated in this window, though.

Summons are creatures that fight for you and can exist in different forms.
They usually come from skilling into their according active skill.
There are different types of Summons:
<b>Devices:</> These are stationary like turrets and traps. Examples are Bladetrap or Sentry.
They usually don't get targeted by enemies, but can get hit by AoE attacks. 
They make use of "Activations" and every attack costs an Activation. Once a Device is out of Activations, it will be destroyed.

<b>Sustained Summons:</> These function like other Sustained skills (like Auras). They reserve a certain amount of Energy or Health. Examples are the Automaton, Core Dweller or Wisps.
They can be toggled on or off in the Sustained Skill Window (which you can access via the Mastery screen).
Sustained Summons usually have passive effects and also an Active component. The active component can be accessed by dragging them into the skill-bar. Most of the time these components cause them to become Empowered or use an ability.
If a Sustained Summon dies, its Restoration Time begins. After that time it will be automatically resummoned. For most of them using the active ability during this time will speed up the Restoration process.

<b>Timed Summons:</> These Summons are actively summoned by the player when using their ability. They usually have a lifetime and disappear after that lifetime expires. An example is the Shadow Clone.

<b>Additional Summon Information:</>
• Summons in general only scale with damage increases that specify them. So "Increased Cold Damage" wouldn't increase a Summons Cold Damage. But "Increased Summon Cold Damage" would.
• Bonuses to "All Damage" include Summon Damage.
• The Damage Bonusses received through the player's secondary Attributes also scale the appropriate Summon Damage.
• Some Attacks of Summons (usually their Basic Attacks) are counted as and thus scale with (Summon) Weapon Damage. Even though the Summon might visually not hold a weapon when doing them.
• Effects that target "Allies" (such as Auras) will impact Summons aswell. So increases to Weapon Damage by Auras will also increase the "Weapon" Damage of Summons.

Crafting allows you to <b>alter</> and <b>improve your items</>.
• It is available at all <b>Blacksmith</> vendors and some others.
• You need <b>Crafting Materials</> based on the item's rarity.
• Most can be best obtained by <b>salvaging</> items at the <b>Blacksmith</>.
• Some Materials, like the rare <b>Vital Flame</> can only be dropped by certain monsters.
• All Crafting Materials tell you how to find them on their individual tooltips.

Crafting Materials can be obtained in multiple ways:
• <b>Salvaging</> items grants large amounts of Materials of the item's rarity and below.
• The same Materials can also be found as loot, but at lower amounts.
• Certain rare Materials, such as <b>Vital Flame</> can only be obtained by <b>killing enemies</> of Tier 3 and above.
You can salvage items and perform crafting at <b>Crafting Vendors</> (usually Blacksmiths).

There are different ways of enhancing your items via crafting:
• <b>Reforge Affix</>: Reroll an affix's numeric value within the same tier. Limited to one affix per item.
• <b>Replace Affix</>: Change an affix to another one from the same pool. Limited to one affix per item.
• <b>Add Affix</>: Adds an affix from the item's possible affixes. Only works if the item hasn't rolled maximum amount of affixes, yet.
• <b>Increase Level</>: Upgrade an item's level to your level. This only increases the value of base stats. Once per item.
Repeatable crafting options have an escalating cost of gold and materials.
Early on they are cheap, so you can make use of them during leveling, even for items you might not want to keep around.
Repeated tries get more and more expensive and are more relevant for optimizing your character later in the game.
You have found a Crafting Material!\r\nYou can use them at <b>Blacksmiths</> to enhance your items.\r\nInitial crafting is cheap, so give it a try even while leveling.
